Sure! It may be a bit long, but I'll try to keep it short.

My brother and his family bought a house in a small suburb as a short sale. They had 2 boys, one was just under 2 when they moved in, the other 7 or 8. Sister-in-law called me a few months later asking about imaginary friends, like if me or my siblings ever had any. Told her no, she went on to say that her youngest son was constantly playing with a little boy and an old man. Mind you, kid was still under 3, so not sure what he would identify as old man at that age. She thought it was a little weird but it happens.

I think it was a few months later, she was asking her son about these "friends". It was getting to the point where you couldn't sit in a chair because they were sitting there. That's when she found out their names, he described them as an old man (which, for a 3-year-old could be anyone over 25) and a boy. They wore overalls and long-sleeved shirts. She asked where they came from and he answered, "They were killed out there a long time ago" and pointed out into the street in front of their house. He said a horse trampled them or something involving a wagon, I don't remember exactly. Just a weird answer for a toddler to come up with.

She still brushed it off as imaginary people, then the night terrors came. I guess the old man started waking up their son in the middle of the night, saying he was going to kill or hurt him. The old man would only come at night anymore and would only be in the nephew's bedroom. After a few sleepless nights, nephew just decided he was going to sleep in his brother's room with the brother, because for some reason, the old man wouldn't bother him in that room. I think it took like a year before brother and sis-in-law just decided the boys should swap rooms. Once the rooms were swapped, everything stopped. Or, nephew just accepted living with these 'friends' and stopped talking about it, or maybe it stopped because they had another baby boy and the baby is the new target? I don't speak to them anymore so I'm not sure.

I did some research on the area. The neighborhood is near a Civil War battleground, and the little subdivision used to be a family farm in the 1800s. There's still the family cemetery just outside their neighborhood, and there are 2 graves that match the names and description (rough age range) of what my nephew hung out with during his toddler years. Couldn't find any obits on those people, though. I think the boy was aged 8 at death and the man with matching name was in his 30's.

Thinking about stuff like this makes me feel sad for people who are so closed minded that they dismiss anything paranormal rather than keeping an open mind. I love that we know so little about the nature of the universe that it's impossible to even guess at what surprises we may discover.

We get the occasional "super-smart" users in /v/Ghosts who make definitive claims (and usually personal attacks) that ghosts can't possibly be real because they believe they know everything significant about the nature of reality... which is basically 17th century Classical Newtonian Physics... and can therefore make claims that an absence of evidence is evidence of absence or that debunking someone's baseless beliefs about ghosts means that ghosts aren't real... in the same way that debunking a child's belief that the moon is made from cheese means the moon isn't real either.

Despite personal experiences, I'm still somewhat skeptical. It's fun to think about all things paranormal, but since these things are not 100% proven, I wonder if there are "real-world" causes for these experiences. Sometimes I wonder if ghosts are just a blip in the dimension of time or something. Things like demons and angels, while terrifying, I'm not sure if those are things the brain manifests or if those beings really do exist.
